key_features.classic_presentation: Small bowel obstruction presents with COLICKY CRAMPING pain that COMES AND GOES IN WAVES (not constant), typically every 4-5 minutes. Pain is diffuse, periumbilical, 6-9/10 severity during cramps. Onset is usually within 12-48 hours. Key associated symptoms: BILIOUS (green/yellow) VOMITING that becomes progressively more frequent and feculent if complete obstruction, ABSOLUTE CONSTIPATION (unable to pass stool OR GAS for >12-24 hours), progressive abdominal DISTENSION (belly swelling). Location: Periumbilical and diffuse cramping, not localized. Key history: Prior abdominal surgery (adhesions most common cause), hernia, prior obstruction. Patient may have TINKLING or HIGH-PITCHED bowel sounds. Key positives: Crampy pain relieved temporarily after vomiting, inability to pass flatus, progressive bloating. Key negatives: Diarrhea rules out complete obstruction. Constant pain with peritoneal signs suggests strangulation (surgical emergency). Blood in vomit suggests advanced obstruction.

red_flags: Severe constant pain with fever and peritoneal signs - strangulated bowel, call 911
Bloody vomit or stool - ischemic bowel, needs immediate surgery
Severe abdominal distension with tachycardia - complete obstruction with possible perforation
Previous bowel obstruction - higher risk of recurrence and complications
